subject: chemistry
stem:
J is a branched-chain alcohol, C₅H₁₂O. J is heated under reflux with an excess of Cr₂O₇²⁻ / H⁺ until no further reaction occurs. An organic compound K is formed in good yield.

The infra-red spectrum of K is shown.

What are the structures of the branched-chain alcohol J and compound K?
stem_lead:
J is a branched-chain alcohol, C₅H₁₂O. J is heated under reflux with an excess of Cr₂O₇²⁻ / H⁺ until no further reaction occurs. An organic compound K is formed in good yield.

The infra-red spectrum of K is shown.

What are the structures of the branched-chain alcohol J and compound K?

options.A: J: CH₃CH(CH₃)CH₂CH₂OH; K: CH₃CH(CH₃)CH₂CHO
options.B: J: CH₃CH₂CH(OH)CH₂CH₃; K: CH₃CH₂COCH₂CH₃

examiner_comment.text:
Question 30

The most commonly chosen incorrect answer was D. From the infra-red spectrum, K clearly has a C=O
group but no COOH group; it is therefore an aldehyde or a ketone. This rules out D. The conditions stated in
the question would oxidise an aldehyde to a carboxylic acid. Therefore, K is a ketone and J must be a
secondary alcohol. The answer cannot be B as this structure does not have a branched chain. Therefore, the
answer is C.

learn_by_solve.solve: K’s IR is C=O without a carboxyl canyon, so aldehyde or ketone. Excess reflux dichromate would oxidise an aldehyde on to an acid, and the question says good yield of K — so K is a ketone and J a secondary alcohol. J is branched C₅H₁₂O. B is unbranched. C fits. Examiner: D was the common error (acid).

options.C: It is reduced to a primary alcohol

followup.why: B is the right chemistry on the wrong skeleton.

followup.why: Examiner: D was the most common wrong answer; the canyon is missing.

examiner_comment.text:
Question 39

The most commonly chosen incorrect answer was C. This was a challenging question involving careful
thought.
• If compound 1 undergoes an addition reaction with steam, butane-1,3-diol is produced. If this is
oxidised, 3-oxobutanoic acid is produced. Statement 1 is therefore true.
• If compound 2 undergoes a substitution reaction with OH
–, 3-hydroxybutanoic acid is produced. If this is
oxidised, 3-oxobutanoic acid is produced. Statement 2 is therefore true.
• If compound 3 undergoes a substitution reaction with OH –, 3-hydroxybutanal is produced. If this is
oxidised, it gives 3-oxobutanoic acid. Statement 3 is therefore true.

All three statements are true, so therefore the answer is A.

Cambridge International Advanced Subsidiary and Advanced Level
9701 Chemistry November 2018
Principal Examiner Report for Teachers

stem:
The infra-red spectrum of compound L is shown.

What could be the structure of L?
stem_lead:
The infra-red spectrum of compound L is shown.

What could be the structure of L?

options.A: HOCH₂COCH₂OH
options.B: HOCH₂CH(OH)CHO

learn_by_solve.solve: Broad alcohol O–H, C–O, no C=O: glycerol HOCH₂CH(OH)CH₂OH. A and B have C=O (ketone/aldehyde); D has a carboxyl canyon.

A.pathway: Student sees C=O and also names a hydroxyketone/hydroxyaldehyde, omitting that an alcohol O–H would still have to be present.

followup.stem: A molecule with both a ketone C=O and an alcohol O–H must show which pair of bands?

options.A: Sharp C=O near 1700 cm⁻¹ only
options.B: Broad O–H at 3200–3600 cm⁻¹ only
options.C: Both a sharp C=O near 1700 cm⁻¹ and a broad O–H at 3200–3600 cm⁻¹

followup.why: Both groups are independent absorbers. Missing the alcohol O–H rules out a hydroxyketone.

B.pathway: Student sees C=O and also names a hydroxyketone/hydroxyaldehyde, omitting that an alcohol O–H would still have to be present.

followup.stem: A molecule with both a ketone C=O and an alcohol O–H must show which pair of bands?

options.A: Sharp C=O near 1700 cm⁻¹ only
options.B: Broad O–H at 3200–3600 cm⁻¹ only
options.C: Both a sharp C=O near 1700 cm⁻¹ and a broad O–H at 3200–3600 cm⁻¹

followup.why: Both groups are independent absorbers. Missing the alcohol O–H rules out a hydroxyketone.

D.pathway: Student treats any C=O as a carboxylic acid and omits the very broad 2500–3000 cm⁻¹ O–H canyon.

followup.stem: Which extra feature, besides a C=O near 1700 cm⁻¹, is required before you can call the compound a carboxylic acid?

options.A: A sharp peak at 2200–2250 cm⁻¹
options.B: A very broad O–H absorption spanning about 2500–3000 cm⁻¹

followup.why: Carboxyl O–H is a canyon from about 2500–3000 cm⁻¹. A ketone has C=O without that canyon.

stem:
Halogenoalkanes can undergo reaction with hydroxide ions.

The reaction of some halogenoalkanes proceeds by the Sₙ1 mechanism.

Which statements about the Sₙ1 mechanism are correct?

RBr + OH⁻ → ROH + Br⁻

1  A carbocation is formed which is stabilised by the inductive effect of the alkyl groups present.
2  Only tertiary halogenoalkanes are hydrolysed in this way.
3  The intermediate formed includes a carbon atom with five bonds attached to it.
stem_lead:
Halogenoalkanes can undergo reaction with hydroxide ions.

The reaction of some halogenoalkanes proceeds by the Sₙ1 mechanism.

Which statements about the Sₙ1 mechanism are correct?

RBr + OH⁻ → ROH + Br⁻

1  A carbocation is formed which is stabilised by the inductive effect of the alkyl groups present.
2  Only tertiary halogenoalkanes are hydrolysed in this way.
3  The intermediate formed includes a carbon atom with five bonds attached to it.

options.A: 1, 2 and 3 are correct
options.B: 1 and 2 only are correct

statements.text: A carbocation is formed which is stabilised by the inductive effect of the alkyl groups present.
Only tertiary halogenoalkanes are hydrolysed in this way.
The intermediate formed includes a carbon atom with five bonds attached to it.

examiner_comment.text:
Question 38

The most commonly chosen incorrect answer was B. Many candidates were unsure of statement 2, which
states, ‘Only tertiary halogenoalkanes are hydrolysed in this way’. The ‘this way’ refers to the S
N1
mechanism.  However, a secondary halogenoalkane can be hydrolysed by a mixture of the SN1 mechanism
and the SN2 mechanism, depending on structure. Statement 2 is therefore untrue.

9701 Chemistry November 2018
Principal Examiner Report for Teachers

subject: chemistry
stem:
J is a branched-chain alcohol, C₅H₁₂O. J is heated under reflux with an excess of Cr₂O₇²⁻/H⁺ until no further reaction occurs. An organic compound K is formed in good yield.

The infra-red spectrum of K is shown.

What are the structures of the branched-chain alcohol J and compound K?
stem_lead:
J is a branched-chain alcohol, C₅H₁₂O. J is heated under reflux with an excess of Cr₂O₇²⁻/H⁺ until no further reaction occurs. An organic compound K is formed in good yield.

The infra-red spectrum of K is shown.

What are the structures of the branched-chain alcohol J and compound K?

options.A: J: CH₃CH(CH₃)CH₂CH₂OH; K: CH₃CH(CH₃)CH₂CHO
options.B: J: CH₃CH₂CH(OH)CH₂CH₃; K: CH₃CH₂COCH₂CH₃

examiner_comment.text:
Question 30

The most commonly chosen incorrect answer was D. From the infra-red spectrum, K clearly has a C=O
group but no COOH group; it is therefore an aldehyde or a ketone. This rules out D. The conditions stated in
the question would oxidise an aldehyde to a carboxylic acid. Therefore, K is a ketone and J must be a
secondary alcohol. The answer cannot be B as this structure does not have a branched chain. Therefore, the
answer is C.

learn_by_solve.solve: K’s IR is C=O without a carboxyl canyon, so aldehyde or ketone. Excess reflux dichromate would oxidise an aldehyde on to an acid, and the question says good yield of K — so K is a ketone and J a secondary alcohol. J is branched C₅H₁₂O. B is unbranched. C fits. Examiner: D was the common error (acid).

A.pathway: Student stops at aldehyde and omits that excess reflux dichromate oxidises aldehydes to acids.

followup.stem: Under the stated conditions (excess Cr₂O₇²⁻/H⁺, heat, until no further reaction), what happens to an aldehyde?

options.A: It is the final product
options.B: It is oxidised on to a carboxylic acid
options.C: It is reduced to a primary alcohol

followup.why: K cannot be the aldehyde. Examiner used this to kill A.

B.pathway: Student picks a secondary alcohol → ketone pair but omits ‘branched-chain’.

followup.stem: J is stated to be a branched-chain alcohol. Is pentan-3-ol branched?

options.A: Yes, any secondary alcohol is branched
options.B: No — CH₃CH₂CH(OH)CH₂CH₃ is a straight chain
options.C: Yes, because it has five carbons
options.D: No, because ketones cannot be branched

followup.why: B is the right chemistry on the wrong skeleton.

D.pathway: Student conflates the acid product of a primary alcohol with the ketone actually on the IR.

followup.stem: K’s IR shows C=O but no COOH canyon. What is K?

options.A: Carboxylic acid
options.B: Ketone (or aldehyde, but aldehyde would not survive these conditions)

followup.why: Examiner: D was the most common wrong answer; the canyon is missing.

stem:
3-oxobutanoic acid can be synthesised in a two-step process.

X → Y → 3-oxobutanoic acid

X → Y → CH₃COCH₂COOH
stem_lead:

X → Y → 3-oxobutanoic acid

What could be the structure of X?

X → Y → CH₃COCH₂COOH

options.A: 1, 2 and 3 are correct
options.B: 1 and 2 only are correct

examiner_comment.text:
Question 39

The most commonly chosen incorrect answer was C. This was a challenging question involving careful
thought.
• If compound 1 undergoes an addition reaction with steam, butane-1,3-diol is produced. If this is
oxidised, 3-oxobutanoic acid is produced. Statement 1 is therefore true.
• If compound 2 undergoes a substitution reaction with OH
–, 3-hydroxybutanoic acid is produced. If this is
oxidised, 3-oxobutanoic acid is produced. Statement 2 is therefore true.
• If compound 3 undergoes a substitution reaction with OH –, 3-hydroxybutanal is produced. If this is
oxidised, it gives 3-oxobutanoic acid. Statement 3 is therefore true.

All three statements are true, so therefore the answer is A.

9701 Chemistry November 2018

statements.text: six-membered cyclic ester containing –C(=O)O– in the ring and a –CH₂OC(=O)CH₃ substituent

examiner_comment.text:
Question 40

Option C was a common incorrect choice. To select the correct option, each compound had to be looked at
separately.
• Compound 1 produces CH
3COOH, CH2OHCH2COOH and CH3OH.
• Compound 2 produces CH 3OH and HOOCCH(CH3)CH2COOH.
• Compound 3 produces CH 2OHCH(CH2OH)CH2CH2COOH and CH3COOH.

Compound 1 is therefore the only compound to produce three different organic products when hydrolysed.
Hence, option D is the correct response.

The products from each compound are those formed by hydrolysis with water or hot HCl (aq). If hot
NaOH(aq) is used, the sodium salts of the acids would be obtained, but the same number of products would
be formed in each case.

Question 2

The most commonly chosen incorrect answer was option C. To produce 800 cm3 of 0.100 mol dm–3 solution
requires 0.08 moles of the specified substance. Since the Mr of (NH4)2CO3.H2O is 114, this appears to be

Question 38

Option A was a common incorrect choice. Candidates were confident that statements 1 and 2 are correct,
but were not as certain about statement 3. If bromoethane reacts with ethanolic KCN, the organic product is
propanenitrile, not ethanenitrile, so statement 3 is incorrect.

3  A six-membered cyclic ester with an O atom in the ring and a carbonyl group adjacent to it; the ring also bears a –CH₂OCOCH₃ substituent.

options.A: 1, 2 and 3 are correct
options.B: 1 and 2 only are correct

statements.text: A six-membered cyclic ester with an O atom in the ring and a carbonyl group adjacent to it; the ring also bears a –CH₂OCOCH₃ substituent.

examiner_comment.text:
Question 40

Option C was a common incorrect choice. To select the correct option, each compound had to be looked at
separately.
• Compound 1 produces CH
3COOH, CH2OHCH2COOH and CH3OH.
• Compound 2 produces CH 3OH and HOOCCH(CH3)CH2COOH.
• Compound 3 produces CH 2OHCH(CH2OH)CH2CH2COOH and CH3COOH.

Compound 1 is therefore the only compound to produce three different organic products when hydrolysed.
Hence, option D is the correct response.

The products from each compound are those formed by hydrolysis with water or hot HCl
 (aq). If hot
NaOH(aq) is used, the sodium salts of the acids would be obtained, but the same number of products would
be formed in each case.

examiner_comment.text:
Question 9

Option A was a commonly chosen incorrect answer. If the numbers from option A are applied to the
equation, there would be no electric charge on the left and a 1– charge on the right. This is not balanced for
charge. On inspection, the oxidation number of chlorine increases by two and the oxidation number of
manganese decreases by three. Therefore, three Cl
 O3– ions are oxidised by two MnO4– ions, hence the
answer D.

Which statements are correct?

1  enthalpy of combustion of H₂ = enthalpy of formation of H₂O 2  enthalpy of formation of H₂ = −(enthalpy of atomisation of H₂) 3  enthalpy of solution of HCl = enthalpy of hydration of H⁺ + enthalpy of hydration of Cl⁻
stem_lead:
Which statements are correct?

1  enthalpy of combustion of H₂ = enthalpy of formation of H₂O 2  enthalpy of formation of H₂ = −(enthalpy of atomisation of H₂) 3  enthalpy of solution of HCl = enthalpy of hydration of H⁺ + enthalpy of hydration of Cl⁻

options.B: 1 and 2 only are correct

statements.text: enthalpy of combustion of H₂ = enthalpy of formation of H₂O
enthalpy of formation of H₂ = −(enthalpy of atomisation of H₂)
enthalpy of solution of HCl = enthalpy of hydration of H⁺ + enthalpy of hydration of Cl⁻

examiner_comment.text:
Question 32

The most commonly chosen incorrect answer was A. The correct answer is D.

• Statement 1 is correct. The complete combustion of one mole of hydrogen produces one mole of water.
• Statement 2 is incorrect. the enthalpy of formation of any element is defined as zero, while the enthalpy
of atomisation of any element that consists of diatomic molecules requires the absorption of a finite and
measurable amount of energy to break bonds.
• The enthalpy of solution of HCl requires the breaking of the H–Cl bond as well as the hydration of the two
ions mentioned, so statement 3 is also incorrect.

9701 Chemistry November 2020

stem:
The unsaturated hydrocarbon octa-1,3,5,7-tetraene, C₈H₁₀, can display geometric isomerism.

How many isomers exist?
stem_lead:
The unsaturated hydrocarbon octa-1,3,5,7-tetraene, C₈H₁₀, can display geometric isomerism.

How many isomers exist?

examiner_comment.text:
Question 20

The most commonly chosen incorrect answer was C.
The double bonds at positions 1 and 7 each have a CH2 group. This will not give rise to geometric isomers, so
these two bonds need not be considered. The double bonds at positions 3 and 5 both give rise to geometric
isomers. The possible isomers might be named, giving the configuration at position 3 first, as cis-cis, cis-trans,
trans-cis and trans-trans. However, if skeletal formulae are drawn and compared carefully it can be seen that
cis-trans and trans-cis are in fact identical. There are therefore three isomers and statement B is correct.

subject: chemistry
stem:
The structure of compound R is shown.

Which statements about compound R are correct?

1  It has an Mᵣ of 116.
2  It contains two groups that show strong absorptions between 1640 and 1740 cm⁻¹ in its infrared spectrum.
3  Its only infrared absorption between 2500 and 3000 cm⁻¹ is sharp and strong.
stem_lead:
The structure of compound R is shown.

Which statements about compound R are correct?

1  It has an Mᵣ of 116.
2  It contains two groups that show strong absorptions between 1640 and 1740 cm⁻¹ in its infrared spectrum.
3  Its only infrared absorption between 2500 and 3000 cm⁻¹ is sharp and strong.

options.A: 1, 2 and 3 are correct
options.B: 1 and 2 only are correct

statements.text: It contains two groups that show strong absorptions between 1640 and 1740 cm⁻¹ in its infrared spectrum.
Its only infrared absorption between 2500 and 3000 cm⁻¹ is sharp and strong.

learn_by_solve.solve: From the structure, Mᵣ = 116 (statement 1). Two carbonyl groups → two strong 1640–1740 cm⁻¹ bands (statement 2). 2500–3000 cm⁻¹ is not ‘only a sharp C–H’: a carboxyl O–H canyon is there, so 3 is false. Key B.

A.pathway: Student treats the carboxyl O–H canyon as a sharp C–H and admits statement 3.

followup.stem: A sharp strong band near 2900 cm⁻¹ is C–H. A very broad 2500–3000 cm⁻¹ absorption is which bond?

options.A: C–H as well
options.B: Carboxyl O–H

followup.why: Statement 3 is false, so not ‘all three’.

C.pathway: Student drops the Mᵣ count (operation on the structure).

followup.stem: Mᵣ is the sum of the atomic masses on the displayed structure. If that sum is 116, is statement 1 true?

options.A: No, Mᵣ cannot be read from a structure
options.B: Yes

followup.why: 1 and 2 are both true.

D.pathway: Student omits the two carbonyls in 1640–1740 cm⁻¹.

followup.stem: Two separate C=O groups each absorb in 1640–1740 cm⁻¹. Does that make statement 2 true?

options.A: No, only one C=O ever appears
options.B: Yes

followup.why: Do not drop statement 2.

subject: chemistry
stem:
The mass spectrum of a sample of neon is shown. The relative abundance of each peak is written in brackets above it.

The graph has the vertical axis labelled relative abundance and the horizontal axis labelled mass/charge. Peaks are shown at mass/charge 20 with relative abundance 100, mass/charge 21 with relative abundance 0.3, and mass/charge 22 with relative abundance 8.

What is the relative atomic mass, Aᵣ, of this sample of neon?
stem_lead:
The mass spectrum of a sample of neon is shown. The relative abundance of each peak is written in brackets above it.

The graph has the vertical axis labelled relative abundance and the horizontal axis labelled mass/charge. Peaks are shown at mass/charge 20 with relative abundance 100, mass/charge 21 with relative abundance 0.3, and mass/charge 22 with relative abundance 8.

What is the relative atomic mass, Aᵣ, of this sample of neon?

examiner_comment.text:
Question 1

The most common incorrect answer was D.
The total abundance of the three peaks is 108.3. The sum which gives the A
r is therefore ((100 × 20) + (0.3 ×
21) + (8 × 22)) / 108.3. The answer to this sum is 20.15.


Cambridge International Advanced Subsidiary and Advanced Level
9701 Chemistry November 2021
Principal Examiner Report for Teachers

  © 2021

learn_by_solve.solve: A_r = (20×100 + 21×0.3 + 22×8) / 108.3 = 2182.3 / 108.3 = 20.15. Examiner: D (21.82) was common — forgot to divide by total abundance.

B.pathway: Student used 108 or 110 as the denominator, or rounded early.

followup.stem: Total abundance is 100+0.3+8 = 108.3. The numerator is 2182.3. 2182.3/108.3 is?
followup.why: Do not replace 108.3 by 100 or 108.

C.pathway: Student picked a visible mass number (21) instead of the weighted mean.

followup.stem: The middle peak is at m/z 21 with height 0.3. Is A_r equal to 21?

options.A: Yes, the middle peak is the average
options.B: No — 21 is almost absent; A_r sits near 20

followup.why: The sample is almost all ²⁰Ne.

D.pathway: Student computed the numerator 20×100+21×0.3+22×8 = 2182.3 and then divided by 100 (or forgot to divide).

followup.stem: After summing m×abundance you must divide by the total abundance 108.3, not by 100. 2182.3/100 = 21.82 is which error?

options.A: The correct A_r
options.B: Forgetting that the abundances add to 108.3, not 100

followup.why: Examiner: D was the most common wrong answer.

Which statements about the reactions of limonene and terpinolene are correct?

2  An excess of hot concentrated acidified KMnO₄ reacts with limonene and with terpinolene to form different diketo acids.

3  The reactions of limonene and terpinolene with an excess of Br₂ produce positional isomers with the same number of chiral carbon atoms.

examiner_comment.text:
Question 37

The most common incorrect answer was C. Each statement will be treated separately.

Statement 1 is true.
Statement 2 is true. When the upper C=C bond is oxidised both limonene and terpinolene give a product with
a ketone group and an acid group in the same positions on the carbon skeleton. However, when the lower
C=C bond is oxidised the ketone group forms on a different carbon atom.
Statement 3 is untrue. Limonene forms a compound with four chiral carbon atoms, as the carbon atom at the
4 position of the six-membered ring becomes chiral. Terpinolene forms a compound with three chiral carbon
atoms.

stem: Which statement is correct?
stem_lead: Which statement is correct?

options.A: 1.0 g of hydrogen gas contains 3.0 × 10²³ atoms.
options.B: 4.0 g of helium gas contains 1.2 × 10²⁴ atoms.
options.C: 16 g of methane gas contains 3.0 × 10²⁴ atoms.
options.D: 44 g of carbon dioxide gas contains 6.0 × 10²³ atoms.

examiner_comment.text:
Question 2
The most common incorrect answer was D.
Since the formula of carbon dioxide is CO2 one mole of carbon dioxide contains three moles of atoms, so D
is wrong. However, since the formula of methane is CH4 one mole of methane contains five moles of atoms,
so C is correct.

examiner_comment.text:
Question 27

The most common incorrect answer was B. The four choices will be looked at separately.

A will be dehydrated under the conditions described to form pent-2-ene. This has cis and trans isomers, so
two organic products are formed.
B will be dehydrated under the conditions described to form pent-1ene and pent-2-ene, so three organic
products are formed.
C will be dehydrated under the conditions described to form 3-methylpent-2-ene and 2-ethylbut-1-ene.
3-methylpent-2-ene has cis and trans isomers so three organic products are formed.
D will be dehydrated under the conditions described to form several organic products, including
3-hydroxypent-1-ene, 4-hydroxypent-2-ene and pent-1,3-diene. This is already more than two.

In a series of nine experiments, to test the reactivity of the halogens, an aqueous solution of each halogen is added to an equal volume of an aqueous solution containing halide ions, as shown in the table.

halogen solution | sodium chloride (aq) | sodium bromide (aq) | sodium iodide (aq) chlorine (aq) | experiment 1 | experiment 2 | experiment 3 bromine (aq) | experiment 4 | experiment 5 | experiment 6 iodine (aq) | experiment 7 | experiment 8 | experiment 9

The nine resulting mixtures are then shaken separately with an equal volume of hexane. The nine tubes are left to stand so that the aqueous and organic solvents separate into layers.

How many test-tubes contain a purple upper hexane layer?
stem_lead:

halogen solution | sodium chloride (aq) | sodium bromide (aq) | sodium iodide (aq) chlorine (aq) | experiment 1 | experiment 2 | experiment 3 bromine (aq) | experiment 4 | experiment 5 | experiment 6 iodine (aq) | experiment 7 | experiment 8 | experiment 9

The nine resulting mixtures are then shaken separately with an equal volume of hexane. The nine tubes are left to stand so that the aqueous and organic solvents separate into layers.

How many test-tubes contain a purple upper hexane layer?

examiner_comment.text:
Question 16

The most common incorrect answer was C.
Since iodine is displaced by chlorine and bromine from sodium iodide experiments 3 and 6 produce a purple
layer. Since iodine cannot displace chlorine or bromine from sodium chloride or sodium bromide experiments
7 and 8 produce a purple layer. When we include experiment 9 this is five test-tubes that contain a purple
upper hexane layer.

Structural isomerism only should be considered when answering this question.

Molecule X contains three C=C double bonds. One mole of X is reacted with three moles of HBr. The carbon skeleton is unchanged.

Displayed skeletal structure of molecule X: two cyclohexene rings joined by a six-carbon chain containing one C=C double bond.

How many different products are formed?
stem_lead:
Structural isomerism only should be considered when answering this question.

Molecule X contains three C=C double bonds. One mole of X is reacted with three moles of HBr. The carbon skeleton is unchanged.

Displayed skeletal structure of molecule X: two cyclohexene rings joined by a six-carbon chain containing one C=C double bond.

How many different products are formed?

examiner_comment.text:
Question 21

The most common incorrect answer was C.
In this explanation it will be considered that HBr adds on to the central C=C bond first.

Cambridge International Advanced Subsidiary and Advanced Level
9701 Chemistry November 2021
Principal Examiner Report for Teachers

  © 2021
Since the molecule is symmetrical it does not matter how the first HBr adds to the central C=C bond. When
the second HBr adds on, the bromine atom can go on either the 2 or the 3 position of the left hand ring.
When the third HBr adds on, the bromine atom can go on either the 2 or the 3 position of the right hand ring.
The four compounds that form can therefore be called ‘2,2’, ‘2,3’, ‘3,2’ and ‘3,3’. Since the addition of the first
HBr made the molecule asymmetrical ‘2,3’ and ‘3,2’ are different, giving four different products.

1  When reacted with an excess of hydrogen and a nickel catalyst, limonene and terpinolene produce the same compound.
2  An excess of hot concentrated acidified KMnO₄ reacts with limonene and with terpinolene to form different diketo acids.
3  The reactions of limonene and terpinolene with an excess of Br₂ produce positional isomers with the same number of chiral carbon atoms.

examiner_comment.text:
Question 37

The most common incorrect answer was A. Each statement will be treated separately.

Statement 1 is true.
Statement 2 is true. When the upper C=C bond is oxidised both limonene and terpinolene give a product with
a ketone group and an acid group in the same positions on the carbon skeleton. However, when the lower
C=C bond is oxidised the ketone group forms on a different carbon atom.
Statement 3 is untrue. Limonene forms a compound with four chiral carbon atoms, as the carbon atom at the
4 position of the six-membered ring becomes chiral. Terpinolene forms a compound with three chiral carbon
atoms.

examiner_comment.text:
Question 38

The most common incorrect answer was B. Each statement will be treated separately.

Statement 1 is true. The three compounds given could form by the cracking of C
12H26.
Statement 2 is untrue. If Y and Z have different Mr values one of them must be ethene or propene, neither
compound shows cis-trans isomerism.
Statement 3 is untrue. If X is octane, Y and Z would both have to be ethene, therefore they would not have
different Mr values.

Question 35

29 per cent of candidates chose the correct answer, A. The most commonly chosen incorrect answer was B.

A molecule of an organic compound, P, contains three carbon atoms and shows a strong absorption at 1720 cm⁻¹ in its infrared spectrum.

P is reacted with an excess of hot acidified potassium dichromate(VI) forming organic product Q.

Q shows a strong absorption at 1700 cm⁻¹ and a strong, broad absorption centred at 2800 cm⁻¹ in its infrared spectrum.

bond | functional group containing the bond | characteristic infrared absorption range (in wavenumbers) / cm⁻¹
C–O | hydroxy, ester | 1040–1300
C=C | aromatic compound, alkene | 1500–1680
C=O | amide; carbonyl, carboxyl; ester | 1640–1690; 1670–1740; 1710–1750
C≡N | nitrile | 2200–2250
C–H | alkane | 2850–2950
N–H | amine, amide | 3300–3500
O–H | carboxyl; hydroxy | 2500–3000; 3200–3600

What is P?

learn_by_solve.solve: P has three carbons and C=O at 1720 cm⁻¹. Excess hot dichromate gives Q with C=O ~1700 and a broad 2800 cm⁻¹ carboxyl O–H: Q is the acid, so P was the aldehyde (propanal). Ketones and 2° alcohols give ketones that do not become acids; 1° alcohol P would not itself show 1720 cm⁻¹ C=O.

B.pathway: Student starts from ‘C=O at 1720’ and omits that the ketone would not oxidise to an acid.

followup.stem: Propanone has C=O. Does excess hot dichromate turn it into a carboxylic acid?

options.A: Yes
options.B: No

followup.why: Q is an acid, so P was oxidisable at the carbonyl carbon — the aldehyde.

options.A: Yes
options.B: No — P already contains C=O, so it is not the alcohol
options.D: Yes, because it oxidises to an acid

followup.why: Right oxidation story, wrong starting functional group.

D.pathway: Student conflates 2° alcohol (oxidises to ketone) with the aldehyde that oxidises to the acid Q.

followup.stem: Propan-2-ol oxidises to propanone, which then stops. Can Q (a carboxylic acid) come from propan-2-ol?

options.A: Yes
options.B: No
options.D: Yes, all C₃ alcohols give propanoic acid

followup.why: Only the aldehyde (or 1° alcohol) yields the acid. P’s own C=O picks the aldehyde.

examiner_comment.text:
Question 5

22 per cent of candidates chose the correct answer, C. The most commonly chosen incorrect answer was B.
30 per cent of candidates chose this answer. The one mole of Zn described in the question has lost two
moles of electrons in becoming Zn2+. The two moles of VO2+ have gained these two moles of electrons, so
the oxidation state of vanadium has decreased by one from +5 to +4. VO2+ is the only ion with vanadium in a
+4 oxidation state, so the correct answer is C.

Question 1

34 per cent of candidates chose the correct answer, A. The most commonly chosen incorrect answer was B.

stem:
When an equimolar mixture of H₂ and I₂ react, the mole fraction of HI in the final mixture is x.

What is the equilibrium constant, Kₚ, for the reaction?
stem_lead:
When an equimolar mixture of H₂ and I₂ react, the mole fraction of HI in the final mixture is x.

What is the equilibrium constant, Kₚ, for the reaction?

options.A: x² / (1 − x)²
options.B: x² / (1 − 2x)²

examiner_comment.text:
Question 13

The most commonly chosen incorrect answer was A. If we assume that the initial number of moles of H2 is 1
and the initial number of moles of I2 is 1 then the equilibrium amounts can be given as H2 = 1-y, I2 = 1-y, and
Cambridge International Advanced Subsidiary and Advanced Level
9701 Chemistry November 2023
Principal Examiner Report for Teachers

  © 2023
HI = 2y, where y is the number of moles of H2 that reacted. The mole fraction of HI at equilibrium, x, is
therefore 2y/2, which simplifies to y, so x = y. This means that Kp = 4x2/(1-x)2.

stem:
X, Y and Z are elements all found within Groups 13, 14 and 15 of the Periodic Table.

X is in the same group in the Periodic Table as Y.

Y and Z are in Period 3.

The first ionisation energy of X is greater than the first ionisation energy of Y.

The melting point of Z is less than the melting point of Y.

Y and Z both form chlorides which are white solids. These white solids react with water to produce solutions with a pH of less than 4.

Which row of the table shows the possible identities of X and Y?
stem_lead:

The melting point of Z is less than the melting point of Y.

Which row of the table shows the possible identities of X and Y?

options.A: X: B; Y: Al
options.B: X: Ge; Y: Si

examiner_comment.text:
Question 16

The most commonly chosen incorrect answer was D. Since X and Y are in the same group of the Periodic
Table, and the first ionisation energy of X is greater than the first ionisation energy of Y, X is above Y in its
group. The answer therefore cannot be B or C. If the answer is D and Y is phosphorus, Z would have to be
aluminium or silicon, but neither element has a lower melting point than phosphorus. If X = boron, Y =
aluminium and Z = phosphorus all the information in the question is correct, so the answer is A.

examiner_comment.text:
Question 3

The most commonly chosen incorrect answer was C. The question hinges on the ability to construct the
balanced chemical equation for the reaction from the information given in the question.
A possible sequence of decisions is as follows:

1. Al
4C3  +  NaOH  →  NaAlO2  this is the information in the question
2. A l4C3  +  NaOH  →  4NaAlO2 balancing for aluminium
3. A l4C3  +  4NaOH  →  4NaAlO2 balancing for sodium
4. A l4C3  +  4NaOH  +  4H2O  →  4NaAlO2 balancing for oxygen – water must be involved
5. A l4C3  +  4NaOH  +  4H2O  →  4NaAlO2  +  3CH4 balancing for carbon and hydrogen gives CH 4

subject: chemistry
subtopic_label: Chemical equilibria: reversible reactions, dynamic equilibrium
stem:
The diagram shows a gas syringe with a free-moving piston. The syringe contains gaseous hydrogen, gaseous iodine and gaseous hydrogen iodide at equilibrium. Three changes are listed. Which changes will result in an equilibrium position at which the rate of the forward reaction has increased?

H₂(g) + I₂(g) ⇌ 2HI(g)

1  increasing the total pressure by adding an inert gas and keeping the volume constant 2  increasing the pressure by adding more gaseous hydrogen iodide and keeping the volume constant 3  decreasing the volume by pushing the piston to the left
stem_lead:
The diagram shows a gas syringe with a free-moving piston. The syringe contains gaseous hydrogen, gaseous iodine and gaseous hydrogen iodide at equilibrium. Three changes are listed. Which changes will result in an equilibrium position at which the rate of the forward reaction has increased?

H₂(g) + I₂(g) ⇌ 2HI(g)

1  increasing the total pressure by adding an inert gas and keeping the volume constant 2  increasing the pressure by adding more gaseous hydrogen iodide and keeping the volume constant 3  decreasing the volume by pushing the piston to the left

options.A: 2 only
options.B: 1 and 2

statements.text: increasing the total pressure by adding an inert gas and keeping the volume constant
increasing the pressure by adding more gaseous hydrogen iodide and keeping the volume constant
decreasing the volume by pushing the piston to the left

examiner_comment.text:
Question 17

The most commonly chosen incorrect answer was C. Statement 1 is untrue as adding an inert gas at
constant volume does not affect the concentrations of the other gases and so has no effect on the rate of the
forward or backward reactions. Statement 2 is true. If hydrogen iodide is added at constant volume
equilibrium is re-established with higher concentrations of all three gases. This means that the rate of the
forward reaction is increased at equilibrium. Statement 3 is true. Decreasing the volume causes a higher
concentration of all three gases.

stem:
When an equimolar mixture of H₂ and I₂ react, the mole fraction of HI in the final mixture is x.

What is the equilibrium constant, Kₚ, for the reaction?
stem_lead:
When an equimolar mixture of H₂ and I₂ react, the mole fraction of HI in the final mixture is x.

What is the equilibrium constant, Kₚ, for the reaction?

options.A: x² / (1 − x)²
options.B: x² / (1 − 2x)²

examiner_comment.text:
Question 13

The most commonly chosen incorrect answer was A. If we assume that the initial number of moles of H2 is 1
and the initial number of moles of I2 is 1 then the equilibrium amounts can be given as H2 = 1-y, I2 = 1-y, and
Cambridge International Advanced Subsidiary and Advanced Level
9701 Chemistry November 2023
Principal Examiner Report for Teachers

  © 2023
HI = 2y, where y is the number of moles of H2 that reacted. The mole fraction of HI at equilibrium, x, is
therefore 2y/2, which simplifies to y, so x = y. This means that Kp = 4x2/(1-x)2.

X, Y and Z are elements all found within Groups 13, 14 and 15 of the Periodic Table.

X is in the same group in the Periodic Table as Y.

Y and Z are in Period 3.

The first ionisation energy of X is greater than the first ionisation energy of Y.

The melting point of Z is less than the melting point of Y.

Y and Z both form chlorides which are white solids. These white solids react with water to produce solutions with a pH of less than 4.

Which row of the table shows the possible identities of X and Y?
stem_lead:
X, Y and Z are elements all found within Groups 13, 14 and 15 of the Periodic Table.

X is in the same group in the Periodic Table as Y.

Y and Z are in Period 3.

The first ionisation energy of X is greater than the first ionisation energy of Y.

The melting point of Z is less than the melting point of Y.

Y and Z both form chlorides which are white solids. These white solids react with water to produce solutions with a pH of less than 4.

Which row of the table shows the possible identities of X and Y?

options.A: X = B; Y = Al
options.B: X = Ge; Y = Si

examiner_comment.text:
Question 16

The most commonly chosen incorrect answer was D. Since X and Y are in the same group of the Periodic
Table, and the first ionisation energy of X is greater than the first ionisation energy of Y, X is above Y in its
group. The answer therefore cannot be B or C. If the answer is D and Y is phosphorus, Z would have to be
aluminium or silicon, but neither element has a lower melting point than phosphorus. If X = boron, Y =
aluminium and Z = phosphorus all the information in the question is correct, so the answer is A.

When ethanol reacts with sodium metal, ethoxide ions, CH₃CH₂O⁻, are produced.

When water reacts with sodium metal, OH⁻ ions are produced.

Which statement about these reactions and the ethoxide ion is correct?

When water reacts with sodium metal, OH⁻ ions are produced.

Which statement about these reactions and the ethoxide ion is correct?

options.A: At the same temperature, the rate of reaction between sodium and ethanol is greater than that between sodium and water.
options.B: CH₃CH₂O⁻ is a stronger base than OH⁻ due to the electron-donating effect of the ethyl group.
options.C: The negative charge on the oxygen in an ethoxide ion is delocalised.
options.D: It is easier to deprotonate ethanol as it is more acidic than water.

examiner_comment.text:
Question 34

The most commonly chosen incorrect answer was C. 21% of candidates chose this answer. C is incorrect
because the ethyl group is electron-donating, this will tend to concentrate negative charge on the oxygen,
not to delocalise it. This has the effect of making the oxygen in CH
3CH2O
– more negative, so CH3CH2O
– is a
stronger base, the answer is therefore B.

stem:
In acidic conditions, iodine reacts with propanone in a substitution reaction.

CH₃COCH₃(aq) + I₂(aq) → CH₃COCH₂I(aq) + HI(aq)

The kinetics of the reaction are investigated using a colorimeter. As the I₂ reacts, the yellow / brown colour of the I₂(aq) fades to colourless, changing the absorbance of the solution. Known concentrations of I₂(aq) are used to prepare a calibration curve graph and the absorbance is then measured as the reaction proceeds.

A graph titled “calibration curve using known concentrations of I₂(aq)” plots concentration of iodine / × 10⁻³ mol dm⁻³ against absorbance, with points (0.1, 0.05), (0.2, 0.10), (0.3, 0.15), (0.4, 0.20), and (0.5, 0.25). A graph titled “absorbance during reaction” plots absorbance against time / s, with points at about (0, 0.5), (10, 0.4), (20, 0.3), (30, 0.2), (40, 0.1), (50, 0.05), and (60, 0.01).

What is the rate of reaction at 20 s?

The diagram shows the mass spectrum of a sample of chlorine. Peaks V, W, X, Y and Z are labelled.

Which statements about this spectrum are correct?

1  The relative atomic mass of chlorine can be calculated from the abundances and m/e values of 2 of the 5 peaks.
2  37.0 g of the species responsible for peak Z contains 3.011 × 10²³ molecules.
3  The relative molecular mass of chlorine can be calculated from the abundances and m/e values of peaks X, Y and Z.
stem_lead:
The diagram shows the mass spectrum of a sample of chlorine. Peaks V, W, X, Y and Z are labelled.

Which statements about this spectrum are correct?

1  The relative atomic mass of chlorine can be calculated from the abundances and m/e values of 2 of the 5 peaks.
2  37.0 g of the species responsible for peak Z contains 3.011 × 10²³ molecules.
3  The relative molecular mass of chlorine can be calculated from the abundances and m/e values of peaks X, Y and Z.

options.A: 1, 2 and 3
options.B: 1 and 2 only

statements.text: The relative atomic mass of chlorine can be calculated from the abundances and m/e values of 2 of the 5 peaks.
37.0 g of the species responsible for peak Z contains 3.011 × 10²³ molecules.
The relative molecular mass of chlorine can be calculated from the abundances and m/e values of peaks X, Y and Z.

learn_by_solve.solve: Cl₂ MS: atomic A_r uses the two atomic peaks (³⁵Cl, ³⁷Cl) — statement 1. Peak Z is Cl₂ molecular ion of the heaviest isotopologue (74); 37.0 g of that species is 0.5 mol of Cl₂ molecules → 0.5×6.02×10²³ = 3.01×10²³ molecules — statement 2. Molecular M_r of Cl₂ uses the three Cl₂ peaks X,Y,Z — statement 3. All three.

B.pathway: Student omits that M_r(Cl₂) is obtained from the molecular-ion cluster X,Y,Z.

followup.stem: The relative molecular mass of Cl₂ comes from which peaks?

options.A: Only the atomic ³⁵Cl peak
options.B: The Cl₂ molecular ions (the three peaks around 70–74)

followup.why: Statement 3 is true. All three statements hold.

C.pathway: Student omits the amount-of-substance reading of peak Z.

followup.stem: If Z is ³⁷Cl–³⁷Cl (M_r 74) but the option uses 37.0 g, that is 0.5 mol of Cl₂. Number of molecules?
followup.why: Statement 2 is true.

D.pathway: Student drops statement 1 (atomic A_r from two atomic peaks).

followup.stem: A_r of chlorine uses the abundances and m/e of the two atomic isotope peaks. Is that two of the five labelled peaks?

options.A: No, you need all five
options.B: Yes
options.C: No, A_r cannot be measured by MS

followup.why: Statement 1 is true. All three.

subject: chemistry
stem:
In acidic conditions, iodine reacts with propanone in a substitution reaction.

CH₃COCH₃(aq) + I₂(aq) → CH₃COCH₂I(aq) + HI(aq)

The kinetics of the reaction are investigated using a colorimeter. As the I₂ reacts, the yellow / brown colour of the I₂(aq) fades to colourless, changing the absorbance of the solution. Known concentrations of I₂(aq) are used to prepare a calibration curve graph and the absorbance is then measured as the reaction proceeds.

A calibration curve graph shows concentration of iodine / × 10⁻³ mol dm⁻³ against absorbance, with points (0.10, 0.05), (0.20, 0.10), (0.30, 0.15), (0.40, 0.20), and (0.50, 0.25).

A graph of absorbance during reaction shows absorbance against time / s, with points (0, 0.50), (10, 0.40), (20, 0.30), (30, 0.20), (40, 0.10), (50, 0.05), and (60, 0.02).

stem:
The diagram shows the mass spectrum of a sample of chlorine. Peaks V, W, X, Y and Z are labelled.

Which statements about this spectrum are correct?

1  The relative atomic mass of chlorine can be calculated from the abundances and m/e values of 2 of the 5 peaks.
2  37.0 g of the species responsible for peak Z contains 3.011 × 10²³ molecules.
3  The relative molecular mass of chlorine can be calculated from the abundances and m/e values of peaks X, Y and Z.
stem_lead:
The diagram shows the mass spectrum of a sample of chlorine. Peaks V, W, X, Y and Z are labelled.

Which statements about this spectrum are correct?

1  The relative atomic mass of chlorine can be calculated from the abundances and m/e values of 2 of the 5 peaks.
2  37.0 g of the species responsible for peak Z contains 3.011 × 10²³ molecules.
3  The relative molecular mass of chlorine can be calculated from the abundances and m/e values of peaks X, Y and Z.

options.A: 1, 2 and 3
options.B: 1 and 2 only

statements.text: The relative atomic mass of chlorine can be calculated from the abundances and m/e values of 2 of the 5 peaks.
37.0 g of the species responsible for peak Z contains 3.011 × 10²³ molecules.
The relative molecular mass of chlorine can be calculated from the abundances and m/e values of peaks X, Y and Z.

learn_by_solve.solve: Cl₂ MS: atomic A_r uses the two atomic peaks (³⁵Cl, ³⁷Cl) — statement 1. Peak Z is Cl₂ molecular ion of the heaviest isotopologue (74); 37.0 g of that species is 0.5 mol of Cl₂ molecules → 0.5×6.02×10²³ = 3.01×10²³ molecules — statement 2. Molecular M_r of Cl₂ uses the three Cl₂ peaks X,Y,Z — statement 3. All three.

B.pathway: Student omits that M_r(Cl₂) is obtained from the molecular-ion cluster X,Y,Z.

followup.stem: The relative molecular mass of Cl₂ comes from which peaks?

options.A: Only the atomic ³⁵Cl peak
options.B: The Cl₂ molecular ions (the three peaks around 70–74)

followup.why: Statement 3 is true. All three statements hold.

C.pathway: Student omits the amount-of-substance reading of peak Z.

followup.stem: If Z is ³⁷Cl–³⁷Cl (M_r 74) but the option uses 37.0 g, that is 0.5 mol of Cl₂. Number of molecules?
followup.why: Statement 2 is true.

D.pathway: Student drops statement 1 (atomic A_r from two atomic peaks).

followup.stem: A_r of chlorine uses the abundances and m/e of the two atomic isotope peaks. Is that two of the five labelled peaks?

options.A: No, you need all five
options.B: Yes
options.C: No, A_r cannot be measured by MS

followup.why: Statement 1 is true. All three.
